items.title: Live: First flight bound for Australia as crisis teams deployed for stranded travellers
items.description: The United States and Israel are continuing to launch strikes at Iran as Tehran becomes increasingly isolated after attacking neighbouring countries. Follow live.

items.title: Marine traffic 'down to zero' due to Middle East conflict
items.description: The Strait of Hormuz normally has 50 ships moving over 100 metres, but today there are virtually zero.

items.title: Australia sends consular crisis teams to Middle East
items.description: The federal government is sending six crisis response teams to the Middle East to help thousands of Australians stranded in the region, while the foreign minister continues to brush off questions about whether the US and Israel's strikes on Iran were legal.

items.title: Stranded Aussies pay thousands in desperate dash home from overseas
items.description: Australian travellers stuck overseas take extraordinary measures to get home amid the escalating war in the Middle East.

items.title: How Iran is hitting a 'vulnerability' of Trump's via the Gulf states
items.description: Despite their immense wealth — and even their past capacity to influence the globe through their control over oil prices — the Gulf states don't have much ability to influence events in this war.

items.title: Live: Albanese says 'no justification' for Iran's attacks on civilian areas
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese calls for Iran to 'cease attacks immediately' on civilian areas. Follow live.

items.title: The Kyle and Jackie O experiment failed
items.description: The network's mammoth deal banked on the fact that people in Melbourne would take to the hosts just as Sydneysiders did.

items.title: Two members of Gus Lamont's family 'not cooperating' directly with police
items.description: South Australia's Police Commissioner has said that two members of missing boy Gus Lamont's family are "not cooperating" with investigators, but a police spokesperson said they could not comment further on the number of suspects in the case.

items.title: Man accused of killing Labor identity Tim Picton freed on bail
items.description: Brodie Jake Dewar, 20, who allegedly killed Labor identity Tim Picton after striking him and causing him to fall over, is granted bail by a Perth judge.

items.title: Dennis Cometti hailed as 'the best of his kind' after death
items.description: Dennis Cometti — who called a range of sports for the ABC, Seven and Nine and was lauded for his football commentary over 50-plus years in the industry — is remembered as "the best of his kind" after his death aged 76.

items.title: Live: Global stock sell-off hits ASX, trade halted in Korea as market plunges
items.description: Investor fears of a drawn-out Middle East war, surging oil prices and potentially higher inflation are hitting Australian shares, with the ASX down 2 per cent. Panic selling hits Korea's market, triggering a circuit breaker. Follow live.

items.title: Giant gas-fired power station planned for power-hungry AI data centre
items.description: A small town in the NSW Southern Highlands is watching the AI revolution take shape in its backyard, as plans emerge to build one of the state's largest gas-fired power stations to run a data-processing complex.

items.title: $15 billion in Australian trade affected by Middle East conflict
items.description: Exports have been halted and shipping containers filled with Australian meat are stranded at sea as the Middle East conflict takes a toll on trade.

items.title: Ecuador launches joint anti-drug operations with US
items.description: Ecuador announces joint operations with the United States to combat drug trafficking, which has caused an explosion of violence in the South American country.

items.title: Your photos of the blood moon from around Australia
items.description: Stargazers across the country have shared photos of the blood moon total lunar eclipse, from the city to the beach and regional backyards — here's a look.

items.title: 'All voices should be heard': Festival presses on after writers exit
items.description: With the potential to be overshadowed by the cancellation of its writers' festival, Adelaide Festival opened over the weekend, bringing together local and international artists.

items.title: Travel quiz: Take a trip around the world with this week's quiz
items.description: Who designed the Louvre's pyramid? And where does pastizzi come from?

items.title: Children's cupcake stand dobbed in to Queensland authorities
items.description: Kelly Stothar says she was flabbergasted when she received a letter from Brisbane City Council threatening her with fines over her children's cupcake stand.

items.title: Long queues at servos as petrol prices surge amid Middle East war
items.description: Petrol retailers across the nation are being accused of "unconscionable" behaviour by preying on people's anxieties as fuel prices surge in the midst of the Middle East war.

items.title: Major search underway on Gold Coast beach for missing tourist
items.description: Police say emergency services were called after reports a 20-year-old man, who is believed to be a tourist, was seen struggling in the water off Main Beach.

items.title: Fringe ticket sales 'drop off a cliff' as fizzer rain forecast combines with cost of living
items.description: A dire weather forecast for last weekend in Adelaide combine with ongoing cost of living pressures to deliver a huge drop-off in Adelaide Fringe ticket sales, organisers and artists say.

items.title: Arrest made in long-running missing persons case of footballer's brother
items.description: Police have made an arrest in relation to the long-running missing persons case of the fraudster brother of a former St Kilda footballer.

items.title: Travellers trapped for days in outback frustrated by lack of communication
items.description: Frustrated travellers say they spent days stranded in outback SA trying to cross the Stuart Highway with no word from authorities.

items.title: War with Iran strains US-UK relationship as Starmer and Trump disagree
items.description: US President Donald Trump has criticised British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer over his reluctance to join the US-Israeli strikes on Iran, saying, "This is not Winston Churchill that we're dealing with."

items.title: US commerce chief agrees to testify on Epstein ties
items.description: Trump appointee Howard Lutnick agrees to a transcribed interview with the House Oversight Committee over his past ties to convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
